note: `overrides` — Elixir HAS the construct: `defoverridable` marks a default implementation as replaceable (26 corpus sites / 14 files) and `super(...)` calls it (17 / 4), and the analyzer read NEITHER before this lane's change. Both mark forms are pinned: `defoverridable f: 1` names the PROVIDER's own f/1, and `defoverridable SomeModule` (the form a __using__ template writes — agent.ex:231, application.ex:416, dict.ex:218, eex/engine.ex:108) names every function of that module, readable only when the module is declared in the same file. Three forbids: a definition whose name is not in the overridable set is a NEW function, not an override (publishing it would be the fabrication the whole ruling turns on); the whole-module form must not fire for a function of a module this file does not declare; and a `defoverridable` inside a __using__ TEMPLATE is quoted code that applies to the module that USES the template, not to the one that defines it — 14 of the 26 corpus sites are that shape (Cc1.WithTemplate pins it, with `template_only` marked ONLY inside the quote so a template-credited mark has an observable consequence). MEASURED AND STATED: the two-endpoint shape is 0 sites in 601 corpus files (probe E8), so `overrides` does not fire on bb_tests/repositories/{elixir,otp}. This fixture is where it fires.
